messages.subject: Extracting area from convex hulls & spatial autocorrelation packages
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I think there's an easy solution to my conundrum, in fact I even had the
nagging sense that I used to know how to do this, but anyways:
Does anyone have some handy R code for calculating the area of a convex
hull? Basically I'm trying to get a rough idea of range size from
species occurrence data.

Also, favorite packages for spatial autocorrelation tests?

THANKS!!
Stella

messages.author: 8d1674b7b16af1b1
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Extracting area from convex hulls & spatial autocorrelation packages
parts:
Searching Google for "convex polygon area R" turns up this function.  It calculates a convex hull and automatically determines the area.  Looks like it has some nice features for discarding outliers as well.  

Looks like there's also a straightforward way to calculate it directly using matrix techniques. Somewhat amusingly, it can calculate negative areas, depending on whether you go clockwise around the hull or counter-clockwise, but that's easy to fix.

I don't know anything about map projections, but I think you'd want to make sure you had an equal-area projection for something like this, to make sure that the area was reasonable.

Robert has some spatial autocorrelation stuff in the dismo package, but I'm not sure if it's related to what you're interested in.

Hope this helps!

Dave
